newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb hits Paris Mosque, one hurt.
newsitem.headline: Bomb hits Paris Mosque, one hurt.

text.p: A bomb exploded outside a Paris mosque early on Monday, damaging the entrance and slightly wounding one man, police said.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the explosion, at 4.30 a.m. (0330 GMT), which shattered windows along the Rue de Tanger in the 19th district of Paris. The wounded man, the guard of the Addawa Mosque, was taken to hospital with injuries to his hand.
Police said the bomb was placed in the entrance of the building, apparently concealed in a fire extinguisher and with a slow fuse. The explosion woke the entire area of the city.
"We have no clues yet to guide the inquiry," one police officer said. Anti-terrorist police were investigating the blast.
Europe 1 radio said the head of the Mosque was known as a liberal who had good ties with other religions and with the local community.

A bomb last December, planted by suspected Algerian Moslem extremists, killed four people in an underground train. Algerian guerrillas accuse France of backing the military authorities in a war against them.
